source_items.title: iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF — Prospectus (Form 424B3)
source_items.publisher: iShares Bitcoin Trust ETF (SEC EDGAR, CIK 0001980994)

excerpts.text: The trading prices of many digital assets, including bitcoin, have experienced extreme volatility in recent periods
Changes in the governance of a digital asset network may not receive sufficient support from users and miners
A temporary or permanent "fork" could adversely affect the value of the Shares
Digital asset markets in the United States exist in a state of regulatory uncertainty

challenges.question: BlackRock's own bitcoin fund prospectus says bitcoin's trading price has seen extreme volatility. If your reason is that bitcoin holds value, how does that fit with sharp drops?
Big funds now hold bitcoin, but the same prospectus says U.S. digital asset markets are in a state of regulatory uncertainty. What happens to your thesis if the rules change?
The prospectus warns that a fork could hurt value, and that governance changes may not get enough support from users and miners. How would you know if that was happening?
I can't verify bitcoin's supply schedule from this source packet. Where did you check it, and does scarcity alone explain the price?
What is one specific thing that would prove your thesis wrong, and how would you notice it?
